content: Magnesium oxide is an antacid that has been approved by the FDA for the treatment of acid indigestion and upset stomach. Common side effects associated with its use include diarrhea and allergic reactions. For adults, the FDA-approved indications include relief of acid indigestion and upset stomach. The recommended dosage for antacid use is one tablet taken twice daily or as directed by a physician. For magnesium supplementation, the recommended dosage is one to two tablets daily or as directed by a physician. The safety and efficacy of magnesium oxide in pediatric patients have not been established. There is also limited information regarding off-label uses of magnesium oxide in both adult and pediatric populations. Patients should not take more than two tablets within a 24-hour period or use the maximum dosage for more than two weeks unless advised and supervised by a physician. Magnesium oxide may have a laxative effect. Patients with kidney disease should consult a doctor before use. Additionally, individuals taking prescription medications should consult a doctor or pharmacist, as antacids may interact with certain drugs. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should seek advice from a healthcare professional before using this medication. Magnesium oxide should be kept out of reach of children. Adverse reactions reported post-marketing include laxative effects. There is limited information available regarding drug interactions, clinical trial experiences, and specific population guidance for magnesium oxide. This includes its use during pregnancy, labor and delivery, nursing, pediatric, geriatric, gender-specific, racial, renal impairment, hepatic impairment, and immunocompromised populations. Magnesium oxide is administered orally. There is limited information regarding monitoring, IV compatibility, chronic overdose, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and nonclinical toxicology. Each tablet contains 240 mg of magnesium and should be stored at room temperature between 59°-86°F (15°-30°C). The product should not be used if the imprinted safety seal under the cap is broken or missing. Patients should be aware that the interaction between alcohol and magnesium oxide has not been established, and they should consult their doctor regarding the effects of alcohol consumption while taking this medication. The brand name for magnesium oxide is MagGel®.
